{{nihongo|'''Juuni Shrine'''|十二神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Jūni Shrine''' (じゅうにじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ar|تيرني (نارا)|azb|تنری، نارا|ca|Tenri|ce|Тэнри|ceb|Tenri (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Tenri|eo|Tenri|es|Tenri (Nara)|eu|Tenri (Nara)|fa|تنری، نارا|fi|Tenri|fr|Tenri|gl|Tenri|id|Tenri, Nara|it|Tenri|ja|天理市|ko|덴리시|mg|Tenri|mzn|تنری، نارا|nl|Tenri|pl|Tenri|pt|Tenri|ro|Tenri|ru|Тэнри|simple|Tenri, Nara|sv|Tenri, Nara|tg|Тенри|tl|Tenri, Nara|tr|Tenri|tt|Тэнри|uk|Тенрі|ur|ٹینری، نارا|vi|Tenri, Nara|war|Tenri, Nara|zh|天理市|zh_classical|天理市|zh_min_nan|Tenri-chhī|zh_yue|天理|qid=Q502196}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}.

It is a candidate shrine for “Yatsugi Shrine” in Yamabe District, Yamato Province, listed as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} (other candidate shrines are {{ill|Yatsugi Shrine|ja|夜都岐神社|qid=Q11431328}} in Otsuki-chō and {{ill|Mirura Yano|Q11431329|qid=Q11431329|lt=Yatsurugi Shrine}} in Taishō-chō).

=== Enshrined deities ===
Its deities are the 11 deities of the {{ill|Kamiyonanayo|Q3275893|qid=Q3275893}} in the main text of the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}, plus {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}; the name “Jūni Shrine” derives from these twelve deities. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was called Jūnisha Daimyōjin.

=== History ===
It is at the northeastern back of the Takenouchi settlement, a rare {{ill|Moated settlements|Q60995739|qid=Q60995739}} in the {{ill|Nara Basin|ja|奈良盆地|ko|나라 분지|ru|Ямато (равнина)|zh|奈良盆地|qid=Q10942269}} located above 100 m elevation. The moat of Takenouchi settlement still remains on the west side.

According to tradition, in the Edo period the precinct of {{ill|Yatsugi Shrine|ja|夜都岐神社|qid=Q11431328}} (ubusunagami of Otsuki Village) was exchanged with Sagizuka Pond in Takenouchi Village, which is the current site of Jūni Shrine. The original ubusunagami of Takenouchi Village was Hakusan Gongen-sha enshrining {{ill|Hakusan Gongen|ja|白山権現|qid=Q11579578}}, but it was {{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|fr|Politique de consolidation des sanctuaires|ja|神社合祀|simple|Shrine Consolidation Policy|zh|神社合祀|qid=Q11590700}} into this shrine in the Meiji period.

=== Precincts ===
There is a sacred stone in front of the worship hall, and a custom of laughing “wahaha,” then circling it three times before worship. Precinct shrines include Nanahashira Shrine and Taga Shrine.

North of this shrine is an area locals call “Hi no Tani.” “Yatsugi” is said to be a changed form of “Yatsurugi,” and because “Hi no Tani” appears often in origin tales of {{ill|Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八剣神社|qid=Q11390593}} in many regions, they are thought to be related.
